corpus.note: The corpus is READ-ONLY. Every question except I40 is pinned to head_commit; I40 is pinned to secondary_commit and is the bitemporal case.

scope.rationale: Agreed with CodeIndexer so the indexed file set and the ground-truth file set are identical. Arc carries near-complete copies of itself under .claude/worktrees; walking them would duplicate almost every symbol and collapse unique-name resolution into ambiguous-name everywhere, erasing the benchmark's signal.
scope.exclude_dir_match: directory basename, at any depth, checked before descending

ground_truth.method: Established by hand with ripgrep plus reading the source. No indexer output was consulted at any point: using the system under test as its own oracle would make the benchmark circular.
ground_truth.semantics: For target T, expect_symbols is the set of function-like symbols that hold a direct static reference to T at depth 1, restricted to the scoped file set. For a trait method declaration, an implementation of that method is a referrer (an `implements` edge) as well as any body that calls it.
excluded_from_the_answer_universe: doc comments and line comments that name the symbol
string literals that contain the symbol name
prose files (.md, .json, .html, .sh, .toml) — outside the extension list
a second extern declaration of the same C symbol
ground_truth.independent_corroboration: mistralrs-core/tests/capability_reachability.rs carries a human-maintained DEAD_SYMBOL_BASELINE cross-checked against rustc's own dead_code pass. Four of the ten zero-callers questions (I27, I30, I31, I32, I33) coincide with entries there. That list was used as a place to look, never as the answer: every line was re-verified at HEAD, and two of its comments were found to have drifted (see the note fields on I23 and I27).

symbol_naming.authority: CodeIndexer, confirmed by running the indexer against arc HEAD 526c909.
symbol_naming.rust: crate name from Cargo.toml with hyphens replaced by underscores, then the module path from the directory under src/ with mod.rs/lib.rs/main.rs collapsed into the parent, then the owning type or declaring trait, then the name. Separator `::`. Trait-impl and inherent methods render identically (no `impl Trait for Type` decoration); a trait method DECLARATION is a separate symbol, so a trait with N implementors yields N+1 symbols sharing a name and N+1 distinct fqns.
symbol_naming.python: dotted; root is the first ancestor directory without __init__.py.
symbol_naming.c_cpp_cuda: namespace + class joined with `::`; file-level module symbols use the repo-relative path minus extension, since C has no module system. A free function in no namespace carries no prefix.
symbol_naming.use: `target_fqn` in questions.json is DOCUMENTATION. It must never be used as a query key — see grade.md section 5, 'Resolving the target symbol'.

known_grading_considerations: 8-candidate ceiling: a call whose name matches more than 8 symbols is emitted `unresolved` (dst null, dst_name preserved) rather than ambiguous, because a 300-element candidate list has no decision value. On the current arc HEAD artifact 9,413 edges are demoted this way; the count is stats.resolution_ambiguity_ceiling. An unresolved edge yields no hop at all, so it costs recall and cannot cause a false-confidence event. grade.md section 5 requires the counter published beside recall.

Confidence ceiling on this corpus: resolution histogram is unique-name 47,564 / ambiguous-name 10,863 / unresolved 44,023, and `measured` is ZERO. Tree-sitter is neither a compiler nor a language server, so the indexer refuses that label rather than inflating it. Every true positive this benchmark can score is `derived` — sound but inferred, not observed. counts.measured === 0 is correct, not a fault.

Query by symbol id, not by name or fqn. An fqn is not unique: loading Arc found seven distinct symbols sharing the exact fqn `vllm::fma` (CUDA overloads across dtype_float16.cuh, dtype_bfloat16.cuh, dtype_float32.cuh). Resolve via /v1/graph/symbols, select on path + line_start, then query with symbol=id:<n>. target_fqn in questions.json is documentation only.

Hop lines are symbol declaration lines, not call-site lines, and the fixture matches: I17's answer QtipBakeConfig::get is recorded at qtip/mod.rs:975 (its declaration) while its call to the target is at :979. Confirmed against a real load, which returns 975.

Trait composition: `implements` edges run Type -> Trait and never name a method, measured on the HEAD artifact. The five trait questions (I22-I26) therefore carry requires_trait_composition, declaring_trait_fqn and a resolution_path spelling out the two hops the runner must take. See grade.md section 5a. A single-hop score on these questions measures the query surface, not the graph.

Language scope: shell, TOML and YAML are not parsed. On I34 the grep-visible `print_banner` call in install.sh therefore produces no edge and the closure is correctly empty — but empty because the language is out of scope, not because the graph outvoted grep. Stated so the report does not overclaim.

Arc HEAD artifact, current: 966 files, 19,177 symbols, 102,450 edges, 3.37 s, 0 parse failures, 126,897 loader rows. Regenerated three times on 2026-08-24 while five CUDA extraction defect classes were fixed; the 19,495 -> 19,446 -> 19,177 symbol drop is roughly 490 fabrications removed, not coverage lost. Any figure captured against an earlier artifact is stale.

Cross-validation of the fixture against the final artifact, read directly rather than through the benchmark. I14 target `qtip_packed_bytes_per_row` (mistralrs-quant/kernels/qtip/qtip_geom.cuh): exactly 1 inbound `calls` edge, resolution `unique-name`, from `qtip_quantize_rows_beam_kernel`. The four `from_env` definitions, keyed by name rather than by sequence because a bare sequence is only meaningful alongside its order: `QtipCodebook::from_env` (qtip/mod.rs:616) -> 1 caller, `get`; `TrellisSearch::from_env` (qtip/viterbi.rs:147) -> 2 callers, `env_search` and `get`; `KvQuantMode::from_env` (models/dsv4_kv_fp8.rs:158) -> 2 callers, `dequant` and `forward`; `EpPlacementMode::from_env` (models/deepseek4.rs:2603) -> 1 caller, `build_expert_parallel_plan`. Every one of those caller names matches this fixture's expect_symbols exactly. Two independent derivations of the same answer sets, one by hand and one by parser, with the hand-built one never having read the parser's output. Hygiene invariants also checked on the artifact: 0 symbol names containing whitespace, 0 phantom `block`/`grid` function symbols.
